In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
The transition to the labour market for young people has become a more protracted and complex process.
The labour market position of young people has improved in the past 30 years, with a reduction in unemployment and an increase in full time employment and apprenticeships.

The youth labour market in the UK has been characterised by high rates of unemployment for young people, and low rates of employment, especially for young people with low qualifications, and for young people from ethnic minorities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evidence shows a significant increase in the proportion of young people who are not in employment, education and training (NEET) in the UK over recent decades.

The labour market position of young people has been improving since the mid-1990s, with a significant reduction in unemployment, an improvement in the employment rate and a reduction in the number of NEETs.
there is no single transition that is a panacea for young people's employment and training outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
young people in the UK have been experiencing a period of high youth unemployment since the early 1990s, and this is a period of sustained youth unemployment that is not seen elsewhere in the OECD.
young people's transition into employment is not a simple one step process, but rather a complex process involving several transitions and a number of different pathways.
the labour market situation of young people has improved since the 1980s, but the improvement has been slow and patchy.
